scenes.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: first full-screen intro artwork for Star Fisher, an Atari VBXE rooftop star-fishing game. Generate one 4:3 landscape image, no collage and no lettering. Scene: a deserted narrow nineteenth-century Paris street at deep night, wet uneven cobblestones leading between tall soot-dark Gothic and Haussmann stone buildings, mansard roofs and chimneys, sparse amber-lit windows and one old gas lamp, a narrow indigo sky above. Subject: a lone adult fisherman walking through the street toward the distant rooftops. He has a long charcoal overcoat, worn black boots, a black round-brimmed hat, and distinctive round antique welding goggles worn over his eyes: dark glass, thick blackened brass rims and small Gothic ornamental pointed details, clearly two individual eyecups, not a welding helmet or sunglasses. Three-quarter side view so his goggles, hat and purposeful walking pose read clearly. His figure occupies about one third of frame height, not a portrait closeup. Carrying a very long slim black fishing rod angled over his shoulder; small reel and thin loose fishing line are readable. Restrained mysterious science-fantasy detail only in the goggles, otherwise period city. Style: grainy old computer adventure-game pixel illustration, low-resolution 320x240 aesthetic with controlled clustered pixels, broken stone textures, subtle ordered dithering, worn engraving-like hatching, readable silhouettes; painterly granular quality of the existing game's dark Paris rooftops, not a clean modern cartoon. Palette overwhelmingly near-black, midnight navy, slate blue, muted grey-violet, only tiny warm amber and pale moonlight highlights. Dramatic depth, atmospheric nocturnal fog at distant street level, quiet melancholic Gothic mood. No bright neon, no contemporary cars, no extra people, no written signage, no interface, no title, no border, no five-point or cross-shaped stars. Full-bleed finished artwork.
